pr_title: desktop/layer_shell: fix centering for opposing anchors
pr_body: Fixes #6160. Tested it with the mako patch mentioned in the issue.
pr_comments: Are you sure this is a regression? Looks like this bit of code hasn't changed in a while, so I think it always worked like this. Should be fixed either way, but would be nice to know what caused it if it changed.

> Are you sure this is a regression? Looks like this bit of code hasn't changed in a while, so I think it always worked like this. Should be fixed either way, but would be nice to know what caused it if it changed.

I never said there was a regression. On taking a closer look, there isn't a difference between sway 1.5.1 and master in case (unlike what I said in the issue). There's only a difference between mako and another client I tested, dunst. Mako shows the surface as if anchored to the left and dunst doesn't manage to show a surface at all, because it immediately gets closed. I didn't investigate it further though.

I now know why the other client failed. It was applying too big of a margin which made the width < 0. I don't really agree with the way that margin is calculated now though.
Now when you have left and right anchors, the margin goes immediately from the width of the surface instead of calculating from the edge of the screen.
For no anchors, no margin is applied.
I'm fine with applying no margin, but if we must (it kinda says so in the protocol), I think we should apply them from the edge of the screen (and do nothing if the window is small enough).

I didn't apply margins for the case where both anchors for now, because I don't know what would be the best way to apply margins there. If you think it makes  sense, I can do `box.x += state->margin.left - state->margin.right` to allow for the use case of offsetting from the center. Other options would be too complicated and less useful I think.
Err, can you rebase to appease the ci? I'm not sure how to tell GH to ignore the test failures from the wlroots version mismatch. Then I can merge it.

> Err, can you rebase to appease the ci? I'm not sure how to tell GH to ignore the test failures from the wlroots version mismatch. Then I can merge it.

issue_context.title: Sway: anchors on opposing sides do not center the layer-shell
issue_context.body:
The documentation of the layer-shell protocol states:

```xml
<request name="set_anchor">
  <description summary="configures the anchor point of the surface">
    Requests that the compositor anchor the surface to the specified edges
    and corners. If two orthogonal edges are specified (e.g. 'top' and
    'left'), then the anchor point will be the intersection of the edges
    (e.g. the top left corner of the output); otherwise the anchor point
    will be centered on that edge, or in the center if none is specified.

    Anchor is double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.
  </description>
  <arg name="anchor" type="uint" enum="anchor"/>
</request>
```

It isn't mentioned that two opposing anchors are not allowed, but when trying
that the window doesn't get accepted. So maybe mention something about that in
the documentation? I would suggest adding something like this:

>     If two opposing edges are specified it will result in undefined
>     behaviour.
comments: Two opposite edges center the surface on that axis.

Well, then consider this a bug report agains sway 1.6.1-rc2 (doesn't seem to be fixed in rc3 from the changelog). The behaviour in 1.6.1-rc2 is different from what I mentioned above (that was 1.5.1).
Namely left-right results in left alignment and top-bottom results in top alignment.
Edit: see this mako patch for a test https://gist.github.com/fwSmit/120497047c1c1d895dd6aa78999825fe

> Two opposite edges center the surface on that axis.

@emersion Hi, where does this quote/conclusion come from? I didn't find anything related to this in the documentation. Should other composers/wayland libraries also follow such conclusion?

review_comments:
If the client requests 0 width and opposing anchors we still need to honor the margin, so we can't drop this.

I'm thinking the cases should really be "if width == 0" and "if left else if right". wlroots guarantees width == 0 implies both horizontal anchors by enforcing the protocol.
Oh right, width = 0 means as wide as possible. I re added it and changed the check to `width = 0` (moving the width changing below).
